item.description: - **The look of Proton Mail.** Proton's purple frame in light and its Carbon theme in dark, a sidebar that lists the panes with counters as Proton's navigation does, warm grey cards, radius 8 buttons, Proton's switch, solid badges and banners. The approval panels show the email the way Proton shows an opened message, and their action bar is Liquid Glass, with a Send button that stays solid purple. Text on Proton's orange is black, as in Proton. - **Postern speaks your language.** The window, the menus, the approval panels and the Touch ID prompts are in English, French, German, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Dutch, Polish, Japanese, Chinese and Korean, and follow the language of your Mac. Counts take their plural forms, and Proton's folders keep the names Proton gives them in your language. Apps still receive Postern's answers in English, the language every model reads best. - **Forgotten files caught in eleven languages.** `w załączniku`, `添付`, `附件` and `첨부` join the words that announce a file, and the confidentiality footers that mention attachments are recognized in more languages. - **The README and the website in the same eleven languages**, with a language menu and links search engines follow. Postern is made in Switzerland, in the canton of Valais.

- **Listed as Proton Mail in your apps.** Postern's entry is now named `proton-mail-postern`, and it introduces itself as "Proton Mail (Postern)", so apps and their tools say which mailbox they reach. An entry made by an earlier version keeps working, and Connect renames it. - **Your settings files stay as you wrote them.** Connecting an app now edits its settings file in place: your comments, the order of your keys, your numbers and your indentation stay, where Postern rewrote the whole file before. - **Hidden text, caught in more disguises.** Styles are now worked out the way a browser works them out: `<style>` rules by importance, specificity and order, then the element's own style, invalid values dropped, comments and escapes decoded, shorthands, custom properties (`var()`) and inheritance followed, nested rules and `@layer`, `@container` and `@supports` blocks read through. On that, text is judged by its contrast with what is behind it in every CSS color form (`rgb`, `hsl`, `hwb`, `lab`, `lch`, `oklab`, `oklch`, `color()`, `color-mix()`, system and named colors, the old `<font color>` rules), at the size it is drawn after zooms and scales, and through filters, transforms, clips, margins, offsets, letter spacing, `content-visibility`, a closed `<details>` or `<dialog>`, and rules for positions or for `:not(:hover)`. Remote background pictures count as not loaded, as in Proton, and pictures carried in the email do not count either: the color behind them does. Gradient and outlined headlines still show. - **A message built to stall the reader is refused.** Before parsing, the page is measured the way the parser builds it; one nested more than 1,000 levels deep, with more than 150,000 elements or megabytes of styles, which no real email has, is not rendered, and the app is told why. Hidden parts are marked instead of removed one by one, every walk through a page is a loop, and thousands of random and broken messages and pages run in the tests. - **Attachments with a stray character are read whole.** A base64 attachment with one character too many at its end, or made of pieces put end to end, used to come out empty.
- **No more emails without their files.** An email whose subject or text says a file is attached (`ci-joint`, `pièce jointe`, `en PJ`, `attached`, `anbei`, `adjunto`, `in allegato`, `em anexo`, `bijlage`…) and carries none is refused before it is saved or shown, so the app attaches what it forgot; `no_attachment` says when no file is meant. Every answer names the files that left, with their sizes. - **Attach files from anywhere an app can reach.** Besides the outbox, `inline_attachments` takes files the app wrote itself (text, or base64 for anything else), and `email_attachments` attaches files of emails it can read, such as an invoice sent on to your accountant. `reply_to_message` and `forward_message` take files too. - **Every draft is checked after it is saved.** Postern reads back how many files Bridge kept; a draft that lost one is removed and the call says so (`attachments_lost`), instead of an email leaving later without them. - **Batches of 5,000.** `create_drafts` and `send_drafts` take up to 5,000 drafts. Approving a batch keeps only each email's digest, and each email is composed again from its draft when its turn comes: thousands of emails never sit in memory, and a draft you change in Proton after approving it does not leave. - **Batches that survive a restart.** An approved batch is sealed on disk as it goes, under a key in Postern's Keychain. After a restart of the Mac or of Postern it comes back in the Overview, and goes on when you choose Resume with Touch ID. An email caught mid-send comes back `uncertain`, never sent twice. - **No second panel when an app calls again.** `send_drafts` answers within a minute, with the outcome or with its batch id while the panel is open, so apps with short timeouts no longer give up and call again; the drafts of a batch stay held until it ends. - **Higher limits for those who need them.** The window now allows up to 300 emails an hour and 1,000 a day (Touch ID), with a reminder that Proton sets its own limits. - **Works with every MCP app.** One click connects Cursor, VS Code (Copilot), Windsurf, Gemini CLI, Kiro and Cline, besides Claude Code, Claude Desktop and Codex (which ChatGPT's Mac app shares). Any other app gets the entry to paste, in its own format: JSON, VS Code, Zed, TOML, OpenCode, Goose, Continue. - **Every model reads every answer.** Claude Code, VS Code and Codex give the model only the structured part of a result, Cursor and Gemini only the text: each answer now carries Postern's sentences in both. Schemas keep to what Gemini and OpenAI's models accept, and the instructions are shorter and depend on the tools you turned on. - **Lighter for the model.** Tool descriptions were trimmed: every tool on now costs about 8,500 tokens, read once. - **A Proton look.** Postern's window and panels take Proton Mail's colors: the deep purple sidebar, the purple accent, Proton's green, orange and red for states, and its badges. - **Updates are named in the window.** When a check finds a new version, a bar at the top of the window says so. - **Postern no longer stays closed after starting on a locked Mac.** macOS keeps the Keychain closed until the Mac is unlocked, so a Postern started then, after an update or a crash, said it was not set up until it was restarted. It now says to unlock the Mac and serves again as soon as it can read its settings.
- **Send from your aliases.** Add an alias of your Proton account under Send from in Postern's window (Touch ID); `send_message`, `create_draft`, `update_draft` and `forward_message` take `from`, replies leave from the address the original was sent to, and `list_addresses` lists them. Any other From is refused (`sender_not_allowed`), and a draft written from an address you did not add is not sent. - **Write drafts from one template, or from a spreadsheet.** `create_drafts` fills `{{name}}` in the subject, body and attachment names with each draft's values, for example one application per company with its own letter. The values can come from a CSV or JSON file in the outbox, one row per draft, as Numbers or Excel export it. Every draft is checked before any is saved, so a missing value or file stops the batch instead of leaving half of it; `dry_run` shows the first draft without saving anything. With `send_drafts`, hundreds of applications take two calls and one Touch ID. - **Sort by search.** The organize tools take `search` instead of ids, to archive, move, label, star or mark as read every message a search finds, up to 1,000 at a time, such as the newsletters older than a month. `dry_run` lists them first and changes nothing. A search must name a condition besides its mailbox. - **Find the people who have not answered.** `awaiting_reply` lists who you wrote to without an answer, the longest wait first: the follow-ups to write, such as job applications with no news. An answer is a reply in the conversation, or a later email from the same address or company domain, Spam included. - **Read attachments without saving them.** `read_attachment` returns the text of a PDF, of a scanned PDF or a photo of a document (recognized on your Mac by Vision), of text, CSV, JSON, calendar and contact files, and of HTML as a person would see it. Everything is read in the sandboxed reader and marked untrusted, like the email it came in. - **Conversations still load when you hide a mailbox.** Hiding a mailbox also hides All Mail, which left every conversation empty; `get_thread` now looks folder by folder then. It also reads only the header of the message instead of downloading it with its attachments. - **Drafts keep their attachments when they are sent.** `send_draft` sent the text of a draft without its attachments, and `update_draft` dropped them too. Both now carry them, the panel lists them, and the bytes that leave are the ones you approved. If you sent drafts with attachments through 0.1.1, check your Sent folder. - **Send a batch of drafts with one Touch ID.** `send_drafts` takes many drafts, or every draft a `create_drafts` batch saved, and shows them all on one panel: who they go to and from, the files and their total size, then each email with its recipients, warnings, subject, the start of the text and its attachments, with a filter to find one. Untick any that should wait, and one Touch ID sends the rest. Each email is still approved for its exact bytes. The tool is off until you turn it on. - **Long batches pace themselves.** Approved emails leave one by one, two seconds apart for a short batch and thirty for a long one (`spacing_seconds` changes it), and when your hourly or daily limit is reached they wait for room instead of being refused. The panel says when the last should leave; `start_at` schedules the first, up to thirty days ahead. The Overview pane follows each batch with a Stop button, and `batch_status` and `cancel_batch` let apps do the same. Pausing Postern holds a batch; a draft leaves Drafts only once its email is sent, and deleting a draft holds its email back. No draft is sent by two batches, each email takes its place in the limits as it leaves, and it carries the time it leaves. - **Attachments from folders inside the outbox**, such as `Letters/Acme.pdf`, and `list_outbox` lists what is there. A file attached to many drafts is read once and held once in memory. - **Clearer sending errors.** An email Proton refuses comes back as `send_refused`, and one whose connection broke while Bridge was taking it as `send_uncertain`, so it is not sent twice by mistake. A batch retries an email Bridge did not take, and goes on past one Proton refused. - **`update_draft` takes `attachments`** to replace a draft's files; without it, they stay. - **Calls are up to 2.5 times faster.** After each call, Postern reread and rechecked its whole activity log, and the next call waited for it. It now checks only what was added since, with a full check every five minutes. - **HTML emails no longer come out empty.** Font size and color are judged where the text inherits them, so a layout that sets a zero font size on a wrapper keeps its text, and rules meant for phones, print or dark mode no longer hide the desktop version. White text on a dark background set by a style sheet stays; text hidden by a style sheet class is now removed too. - **Calls made at the same time no longer hang.** Two apps, or one app calling two tools at once, could leave a call waiting until the client gave up. Postern now runs them one after the other on its Bridge session.

Postern now updates itself.
- **Check for Updates** in the Postern menu and in the menu bar icon's menu. When a version is waiting, both items name it. - **Automatic checks only if you say yes.** Postern asks once, over its window; Security › Updates changes it later. Once a day, it reads the list of versions on getpostern.vercel.app and downloads updates from GitHub. - **Signed end to end.** The list of versions and every update are signed with Postern's own key (EdDSA), checked before anything is opened, and nothing installs until you click Install and Relaunch. - **The only connection besides Bridge**, now named in the threat model with what it reveals: your IP address and Postern's version, nothing else.
